Brent oil price increased by 2.17% to $75.77, while gold fell by 0.24% to $4135.50. The 10-year US bond yield rose by 0.98% to 4.52%. market_impact_summary.en: The stock market was influenced by geopolitical news and central bank decisions. The S&P 500 fell by 0.45% to 7503.85, while the Nikkei closed down 2.11% at 66,819. The oil price and the increase in bond yields contributed to market caution.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in calo del 2,11%, Shanghai in ribasso dello 0,49%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura debole per i mercati europei.

Il S&P 500 è in calo dello 0,45% a sette‑mila‑cinquecentotre‑punto‑ottantacinque. Il VIX è in rialzo dell'1,80% a sedici‑punto‑quarantadue, segnale di propensione al rischio. Il Dollar Index è in calo dello 0,17% a cento‑punto‑novantasei, riflette una leggera pressione sul dollaro. L'oro è in ribasso dello 0,24% a quattro‑mila‑centotrentacinque‑punto‑cinquanta dollari l'oncia. Il Brent è in rialzo del 2,17% a settantacinque‑punto‑settantasette dollari, spinto da tensioni geopolitiche. Il rendimento dei titoli USA a dieci anni è in rialzo dello 0,98% a quattro‑virgola‑cinquantadue percento, indicatore di aspettative inflazionistiche più elevate. Il rendimento dei BTP a dieci anni è stabile al 3,82%.

Nel contesto geopolitico, la riemersione dei pirati somali riaccende le preoccupazioni sulla sicurezza marittima nell'Oceano Indiano, potenzialmente influenzando i costi di assicurazione e le rotte commerciali. Inoltre, il prossimo summit NATO potrebbe delineare nuove linee di difesa contro le minacce cyber‑elettriche, con possibili ripercussioni sui mercati energetici.

Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi. La sola notizia di rilievo è il commento del capo della banca centrale della Nuova Zelanda, che celebra una ripresa della crescita, ma senza impatto immediato sui mercati europei o statunitensi.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin registra una leggera flessione dello 0,35% a sessantaduemilanovecentoventuno dollari. Gli ETF su Bitcoin hanno registrato un afflusso netto di duecentosessantacinque virgola sette milioni di dollari, segnale di interesse istituzionale. Ethereum scende dello 0,87% a milleseicento cinquantaquattro dollari, mentre Solana registra una perdita significativa del quattro virgola zero quattro per cento, attestandosi a settantotto dollari e sedici centesimi. Il Fear & Greed Index è a venti, classificato come paura estrema, suggerendo cautela sugli investitori.

Nessun dato macro in agenda oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing.

The Nikkei closed down 2.11%, Shanghai down 0.49%. This suggests a weak opening for European markets.

The S&P 500 is down 0.45% at 7,503.85. The VIX is up 1.8% at 16.42, a signal of risk appetite. The Dollar Index is down 0.17% at 100.96, reflecting slight pressure on the dollar. Gold is down 0.24% at $4,135.5 an ounce. Brent is up 2.17% at $75.77, driven by geopolitical tensions. The U.S. 10‑year Treasury yield is up 0.98% at 4.52%, an indicator of higher inflation expectations. The 10‑year BTP yield is stable at 3.82%.

In the geopolitical context, the re‑emergence of Somali pirates reignites concerns over maritime security in the Indian Ocean, potentially affecting insurance costs and trade routes. Additionally, the upcoming NATO summit could outline new defenses against cyber‑electric threats, with possible repercussions for energy markets.

No significant macro data scheduled for release today. The only notable news is the comment from the head of the New Zealand central bank, celebrating a rebound in growth, but with no immediate impact on European or U.S. markets.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin is down 0.35% at $62,921. Bitcoin ETFs saw a net inflow of $265.7 million, a sign of institutional interest. Ethereum falls 0.87% to $1,654, while Solana records a significant loss of 4.04%, sitting at $78.16. The Fear & Greed Index is at 20, classified as extreme fear, suggesting investor caution.

No macro data on the agenda today. To dive deeper into today's topics, visit our platform for the full articles in the Top Stories section. Thank you for listening and see you tomorrow.

articles.title: What to Expect at the NATO Summit
articles.snippet: As NATO prepares for its 2026 summit, European members’ immediate concerns centre less on what to do about Ukraine than on whether the U.S. president might spoil the intended show of unity. In this Q&A, Crisis Group expert Olga Oliker previews the alliance’s annual gathering.

articles.summary_en: The NATO summit will be held soon and there will be discussions on European security and the war in Ukraine.

articles.title: Gathering Clouds: Building Digital Strategic Depth in the Compute Age
articles.snippet: The wars in Ukraine and the Middle East have exposed a strategic reality that military planners are only beginning to confront: In a data-centric age, digital infrastructure has become part of the battlespace. Data centers and cloud regions are now the digital backbone of military power and economic prosperity. As such, they present attractive targets for rapidly proliferating long-range strike systems, drones, and cyber capabilities. articles.title: Inside Ukraine’s Game-Changing Drone Industry
articles.snippet: In recent months, Ukrainian drones have successfully struck dozens of sites deep inside Russia, targeting the oil industry, weapons plants, and logistics hubs. But while Ukraine has developed a world-leading military technology to defend itself from a much larger aggressor, drones will not be enough to end the war.
articles.summary_it: L'Ucraina ha sviluppato una tecnologia di droni di classe mondiale per difendersi da un aggressore molto più grande.
articles.summary_en: Ukraine has developed world-leading drone technology to defend itself from a much larger aggressor.

articles.title: Somali Pirates Are Back — But the Coalition That Beat Them Isn’t Coming
articles.snippet: Numerous recent pirate attacks, especially the hijacking of three merchant vessels off the Horn of Africa, are a stark reminder that the conditions for resurgence can return quickly.It took years of sustained, coordinated effort by multinational naval coalitions, the shipping industry, and international organizations to get rid of pirates in the Western Indian Ocean and the Gulf of Aden. Since 2016, many observers have viewed Somali piracy as yesterday’s problem. Shipping companies increasingly treated the threat as manageable, and Western navies no longer prioritized it. However, piracy did not disappear, it simply went dormant. articles.title: The Missing Ingredient for European Tech Sovereignty
articles.snippet: Europe’s dependence on US technology companies is both an economic challenge and a strategic vulnerability. The European Union’s new Tech Sovereignty Package is a step in the right direction, but without equally ambitious efforts to curb market concentration, it is bound to fall short.

This could be a problem for President Trump who has already slammed Big Oil for keeping prices at the pump too high. The two biggest American oil companies are reporting second-quarter results at the end of this month and, according to Reuters, will book the best quarter since 2022, when Western sanctions on Russia following its incursion into Ukraine…

articles.title: The Next Oil Price Spike Could Come Sooner Than Traders Think
articles.snippet: Oil prices have dropped back to pre-war levels since the United States and Iran agreed to negotiate a deal under a framework that included the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. With oil flows out of the Middle East starting to return to the market, analysts, investment banks, and traders expect the global oil glut to return as early as in 2027 and sink oil prices further. Prices are heading south to $60 per barrel, many analysts think. The futures market seems to think this way, too. Speculators are betting on where they think prices will go in…
